自鳴弦琴亦稱鼓齊特琴，見於印度洋地區、非洲及其流散地區、歐洲與北美。竹製者包括馬: The idiochord, also called the drum zither, is found in the Indian Ocean region, Africa and its diaspora, Europe and North America. Bamboo examples include the valiha of Madagascar, the kulibit of the Philippines and Indonesia and the karaniing of the Mon-Khmer-speaking peoples of Malaysia; the benta of Jamaica is a large single-string bamboo instrument played with a slide. There are also cornstalk fiddles and single-string instruments made from the ribs of sago palm leaves and from ita palm fibre, found in North America, the Carpathians, Serbia, eastern New Guinea, Venezuela and Guyana; the akadingidi of Uganda and the mpeli of the Congo and the Central African Republic belong here too.
自鳴弦琴多地分散發展，見於印度洋、非洲及其散居地、歐洲與北美。其變化在於以同一材: The idiochord developed separately in many places, and is found in the Indian Ocean, Africa and its diaspora settlements, Europe and North America. What varies is that the string is made of the same material as the body, and that local materials led to forms in bamboo tube, cornstalk, leaf rib and leaf fibre. Bamboo forms are common: the middle of a bamboo tube is cut open, leaving the ends as the string, and a stick is inserted as the bridge; the valiha of Madagascar, the kulibit of the Philippines and Indonesia and the karaniing of Malaysia are of this kind. The benta of Jamaica is a large single-string bamboo instrument played with a slide. Other examples include cornstalk fiddles in North America, the gingara of the Carpathians and Serbia, a single-string instrument of sago palm leaf rib in eastern New Guinea, a single-string instrument of ita palm fibre among the Warao of Venezuela and Guyana, and the akadingiti of Uganda and the mpeli of the Congo and the Central African Republic.

Some single-string bamboo instruments change pitch by sliding. The source does not describe the range or how volume is controlled, nor the difference in timbre from related instruments.

The idiochord, also called the drum zither, is a chordophone whose 'string' is cut from the same material as the resonating body rather than being fitted separately. It is commonly made by cutting the skin from the middle of a bamboo tube to form the string, still joined at both ends, and propping it up on a small stick as a bridge. It is distributed across the Indian Ocean, Africa and its diaspora settlements, Europe and North America. The valiha of Madagascar, the kulibit of the Philippines and Indonesia, the karaniing of Malaysia and the benta of Jamaica are all of this kind; the benta is played with a slide. There are also methods using cornstalk, sago palm rib and leaf fibre.
製作自鳴弦琴時，可取竹管、玉米稈或葉脈等材料，在中段剖出或挑起一條與共鳴體同材質: To make an idiochord, take a bamboo tube, cornstalk or leaf vein, cut or lift out a strip of fibre of the same material as the resonating body, leaving both ends joined, then insert a small stick underneath as a bridge to raise the fibre. As for playing, the source states clearly only that the benta of Jamaica changes pitch by sliding a stick along the string; other details of sound production are not given. For a beginner the points are not to cut through the two ends, to keep the bridge firm, and to check that string and body are of the same material.
